s01.narration: Want your recruitment set up exactly the way it really works at your company? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you how to customize the ATS module.

s02.narration: In the left menu, in the Company section, I click ATS.

s03.narration: Overview and administration opens, with the Jobs, All candidates and Talent pool tabs.

s04.narration: Opening positions and working with candidates are covered in two other videos, and here we'll look at the settings that apply to all positions.

s05.narration: The Job portal button opens your public career page, where applicants find your open positions.

s06.narration: At the top right I click the Settings button.

s07.narration: On the left is a menu with every settings area, from the portal address all the way to the thank you message.

s08.narration: In Portal URL, in the Domain field, you choose what the link to your career page will look like.

s09.narration: In the GTM id field you paste the code from Google Tag Manager to measure traffic on the page.

s10.narration: I click Embed code, where you'll find the code for embedding the career page directly on your company website.

s11.narration: You choose the language and look of the page, and hand the code to your web admin with the Copy button.

s12.narration: Now I click Recruitment stages, which every candidate goes through.

s13.narration: Stages are in three groups: Candidate in hiring, Candidate hired and Candidate not hired.

s14.narration: Stages in the Candidate not hired group serve as rejection reasons, for example an unsuitable candidate or a candidate who turned down the offer.

s15.narration: At the top you change the group's color with the brush, and you reorder stages by dragging the handle on the left.

s16.narration: I add a new stage with the Add new stage button in the Candidate in hiring group.

s17.narration: In Name I type Phone screening – demo and click Save.

s18.narration: The new stage has been added at the end of the group and will be offered whenever you create a new job position.

s19.narration: I click the three dots next to it, where you can rename the stage, delete it or set an automatic email for it.

s20.narration: In the menu I click Set automatic email.

s21.narration: An active email would go to every candidate who moves to this stage, so I'll leave it inactive.

s22.narration: In Subject I type Invitation to a short phone call.

s23.narration: In Message I type Hello, and on the right under Variables I click Candidate name.

s24.narration: I click Preview, and a sample candidate name appears in the text instead of the variable.

s25.narration: I won't save the template now, so I click Cancel.

s26.narration: I click Company details, where you write the text shown below the description of every position.

s27.narration: I click GDPR consents, where you'll find the consent text that applicants must confirm on the career page.

s28.narration: By ticking Talent pool consent, you ask applicants to let their details stay in the talent pool for future hiring too.

s29.narration: Below that you set how long the consent is valid and whether a notification should be sent fourteen or thirty days before it expires.

s30.narration: I click Company photos, where you upload photos from the office or team events for your job ads.

s31.narration: I click Talent pool categories, which you use to sort people in your talent pool.

s32.narration: I click Candidate sources, the labels that tell you where candidates came from, for example LinkedIn or Startupjobs.

s33.narration: I click Add and type Job fair – demo as the name.

s34.narration: I click Save, and you can then assign the new label to candidates who came from the job fair.

s35.narration: I click AI matching, where you can turn on highlighting of the applicants who best match the position.

s36.narration: Finally I click Thank you message, which every applicant receives right after sending their application.

s37.narration: I click Back, and I'm in the job overview again.

s38.narration: Now your career page, recruitment stages, consents and candidate sources are ready, and if something doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s39.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
